original_question: For every n >= 2 and d >= 3, prove both of the following conditions used to establish Conjecture 1.1: first, the morphism P∇|P X_n^d from P X_n^d // SL_n to Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n is a closed immersion, meaning an isomorphism onto a closed subset; second, the morphism PΨ from Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n to P C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)}^{ss} // SL_n is an isomorphism onto a closed subset of an affine open subset.
target_in_paper: Proposition 1.2 together with Theorem 1.3. More precisely, your draft is trying to capture the two-step reduction of Conjecture 1.1 in the paper: Proposition 1.2 reduces Conjecture 1.1 to proving that the induced morphism coming from the projectivized gradient map is a closed immersion, while Theorem 1.3 supplies the corresponding statement for the associated-form morphism. The paper-faithful remaining research question is therefore the first condition only.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the two morphisms that are central to the paper’s reduction of Conjecture 1.1, namely the projectivized gradient morphism and the projectivized associated-form morphism, and it correctly phrases the desired geometric properties on GIT quotients in terms of closed immersions / isomorphisms onto closed subsets. It also correctly recognizes that these statements are used to attack Conjecture 1.1.
missing_details: The base field is C throughout.
The ambient vector space of degree-d forms must be specified, e.g. Q_n^d = C[z_1, ..., z_n]_d (or the paper’s equivalent notation), together with X_n^d = {f in Q_n^d : Delta(f) != 0}.
The projectivized domain P X_n^d must be defined explicitly as the open subset of P(Q_n^d) consisting of forms with nonvanishing discriminant.
The gradient morphism must be defined explicitly by [f] |-> <partial f/partial z_1, ..., partial f/partial z_n>.

The target Z_n^{d-1} must be defined: it is not an arbitrary quotient space, but the image/locus of balanced complete intersections arising from the projectivized gradient map in the appropriate Grassmannian or its GIT quotient.

The associated-form morphism Psi must be defined explicitly in terms of the Macaulay inverse system / associated form of a balanced complete intersection of type (d-1, ..., d-1), with resultant nonzero and socle degree n(d-2).
The semistable locus in P(C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)}) must be stated explicitly, since the quotient in the codomain of P Psi is the GIT quotient of the semistable locus.
It should be stated that all quotients are GIT quotients by SL_n, not arbitrary orbit spaces.
The phrase 'closed immersion' should be tied to the paper’s moduli/GIT context: an isomorphism onto a closed subvariety of the target quotient.
The phrase 'isomorphism onto a closed subset of an affine open subset' should be tied to the specific affine open subset singled out in Theorem 1.3.
Your draft broadens the paper’s actual open target: Theorem 1.3 already proves the second statement, so the remaining problem isolated by the paper is the first statement.

To make the question fully stand-alone, it should also recall Conjecture 1.1 itself: every regular GL_n-invariant function on X_n^d should arise as the pullback, via the associated-form morphism, of a rational invariant on the target defined on the image.
The quantifiers n >= 2 and d >= 3 should be attached to all notation and maps at the moment they are introduced, not only at the start.
refined_question: Over C, let Q_n^d := C[z_1, ..., z_n]_d, let X_n^d := {f in Q_n^d : Delta(f) != 0}, and let P X_n^d be its projectivization inside P(Q_n^d). For [f] in P X_n^d, define the projectivized gradient morphism by P∇([f]) := <partial f/partial z_1, ..., partial f/partial z_n>, viewed as a point of the Grassmannian of n-dimensional subspaces of Q_n^{d-1}; let Z_n^{d-1} denote the induced SL_n-invariant image/locus of balanced complete intersections of type (d-1, ..., d-1). Let PΨ be the projectivized associated-form morphism sending a balanced complete intersection with nonzero resultant to its Macaulay inverse system (equivalently, associated form) in P(C[e_1, ..., e_n]_{n(d-2)}), and let the codomain quotient be taken on the semistable locus. Is the induced morphism of GIT quotients P∇|_{P X_n^d} : P X_n^d // SL_n -> Z_n^{d-1} // SL_n a closed immersion for every n >= 2 and d >= 3? By Proposition 1.2 together with Theorem 1.3, an affirmative answer would provide the remaining step in the paper’s reduction of Conjecture 1.1.
justification: The draft is close to the paper’s Section 1 reduction strategy, but it is not fully paper-faithful because it asks to prove both geometric input statements, whereas the paper separates them: Proposition 1.2 explains that Conjecture 1.1 would follow from the closed-immersion property of the projectivized gradient morphism together with the geometric statement about PΨ, and Theorem 1.3 supplies the latter. Thus the sharp stand-alone research question, staying as close as possible to the paper’s actual intent, is the first condition only, with all notation and GIT hypotheses made explicit. The nearby context in Sections 2 and 3 is needed because that is where the paper defines the associated form of a balanced complete intersection, the map Psi, and the projective/GIT setup in which Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 are formulated.
